issues.issue: Whether 12,666 of workers' compensation that offset 2019 SS benefits is a 'social security benefit' (benefits treated as received = 19,866)
issues.lean: not modelled; court's 19,866 encoded as socialSecurity
issues.diagnosis: Legal characterisation under 86(d)(3), and the IRS concession excluding 35,382 of retroactive 2016-2018 benefits, are done outside the framework; only the resulting amount is an input.
issues.snippet: under section 86(d) petitioners are nonetheless required to treat this sum as Social Security benefits for Federal income tax purposes

issues.court: 16,886 (85% x 19,866; parties agree the 85% ratio applies); 11,684 over the 5,202 reported
issues.lean: 0 with only the found income (interest 33, dividends 38); 16,886 in labelled sensitivity runs at non-SS MAGI 46,874 and 46,875
issues.diagnosis: Missing facts, not a framework error: the opinion states no other income. The 85% cap binds iff 0.85 x (MAGI + 9,933 - 44,000) + 6,000 >= 16,885.5, i.e. MAGI >= 46,874 (MFJ, nearest-dollar). As filed, 5,202 = 85% of 6,120 requires MAGI >= 43,460 (0.85 x (M + 3,060 - 44,000) + 3,060 >= 5,202). The court adopts the ratio by agreement, not computation.
issues.snippet: Respondent contends that the 85% inclusion ratio applies here, and petitioners do not appear to disagree.

issues.diagnosis: Concession encoded; reported interest/dividend totals unknown, so only the omitted amounts are encoded.

Respondent has also conceded the accuracy-related penalty.
